The series follows archaeologists and students at a Greek site whose find of a rare artifact triggers an international adventure filled with conspiracy. It stars Poehler as site manager Elise alongside Hugh Laurie as her boss Neville and features several other key performers in an intergenerational workplace setting.

The 10-episode comedy series Dig reached Peacock on November 23 with every installment available at once for immediate viewing. Created by Amy Poehler and Mike Schur from Kate Myers' novel Excavations, the show places its characters at an archaeological dig in Greece where a rare artifact surfaces and pulls the group into a wider conspiracy.

Amy Poehler plays Elise, the site manager who keeps the operation running. Hugh Laurie appears as her boss Neville. Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas and Fina Strazza fill out the core group of archaeologists and students. Guest performers include Kayvan Novak, Jon Pointing, Bonita Friedericy, Jason Mantzoukas, Brennan Lee Mulligan and Max Greenfield.

Co-showrunners Michael Schur and J.J. Philbin oversaw production through Universal Television along with Paper Kite Productions and 3 Arts Entertainment. The story leans on familiar discovery tropes yet centers the daily rhythms of the team, letting small interactions and shared problem-solving carry the momentum rather than manufactured rivalries.

By November 24 all ten episodes remained ready to stream on the platform. The format revives the pleasures of an ensemble workplace comedy transplanted to an adventurous setting, where character choices and collective ingenuity matter more than isolated heroics.

seltz.title: A Penn grad thought archaeology was boring. Now Amy Poehler is starring in a comedy inspired by her experience.
seltz.snippet:
In the summer of 2008, Kate Myers embarked on an archaeological trip to southern Greece.

Then a recent University of Pennsylvania graduate, Myers worked long hours in the sweltering Mediterranean heat at one of Penn’s international digs. She had always dreamed of unearthing centuries-old artifacts at excavation sites around the world but soon realized that the strenuous digging for relics beneath layers of hard-packed soil wasn’t quite the career she wanted.

She certainly didn’t expect that the experience would one day inspire a comedy series starring Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie.

*Dig*, a new Peacock comedy based on Myers’ debut novel, *Excavations*, is now streaming all 10 episodes.

“I was 22 and had no idea what I was doing,” she said. “And because it takes so long to find anything, these projects are like generational digs. I found that pretty boring. But some people like that it’s layer by layer, and very methodical.”

After she returned home, Myers moved to New York City and then Los Angeles to work in TV development. She was tasked with creating new show ideas and discovering books with potential to turn into hit adaptations.

Years of scouring other people’s books inspired Myers, who was born in Bryn Mawr and grew up in Maryland, to write her own.
